question: 15 mangoes are bought for ₹250, and 9 mangoes are bought for ₹200. If all the mangoes are sold at ₹240 per dozen, then what is the profit percentage in the entire transaction (round up to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP for 24 mangoes (2 dozen) = 250 + 200 = ₹450

Total SP for 2 dozen mangoes = 2 × 240 = ₹480

Profit = 480 − 450 = ₹30

Profit % = (30 ÷ 450) × 100 = 6.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 15 mangoes = ₹250

Cost of 9 mangoes = ₹200

Selling price of mangoes per dozen (12 mangoes) = ₹240

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
